chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who has a debt: “Is hajj obligatory upon him?” He said:

“Yes. Indeed, the hajj of Islam is obligatory upon whoever among the Muslims is able to walk. Most of those who performed hajj with the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله were walking. And the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله passed by Kurāʿ al-Ghamīm, and they complained to him of strain, exertion, and fatigue. So he said, ‘Tighten your waist-wraps and bind your stomachs.’ They did that, and that went away from them.”

key_terms.حَجَّةَ الْإِسْلَامِ: the obligatory hajj incumbent in Islam

ai.seo_question: Is hajj obligatory for someone who has debt if he is physically able to walk?
ai.summary: This hadith states that hajj remains obligatory for a Muslim who is able to make the journey on foot, even if he has debt. It also cites the practice of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his companions, showing endurance in travel and the physical discipline used to bear hardship.
